'''''Stellaria alsine''''', the '''bog stitchwort''', is a species of herbaceous perennial [[flowering plant]] in the carnation family [[Caryophyllaceae]]. It grows in bogs and marshes in Europe and parts of North America.

==Description==
Bog stitchwort is a [[rhizome|rhizomatous]] [[perennial plant]], with smooth, four-angled stems up to {{convert|40|cm|abbr=on}} tall.<ref name="FNA">{{cite book |series=Flora of North America |volume=5 |title=Magnoliophyta: Caryophyllidae, Part 2 |editor=Flora of North America Editorial Committee |publisher=[[Oxford University Press]] |year=1993 |isbn=978-0-19-522211-1 |chapter=''Stellaria'' Linnaeus, Sp. Pl. 1: 421. 1753. Gen. Pl. ed. 5, 193. 1754 |first=John K. |last=Morton |pages=99–114 |chapter-url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=200007067}}</ref> Its leaves are opposite and narrow, up to {{convert|13|mm|abbr=on}} long, with untoothed margins but a few marginal hairs towards the leaf-base.<ref name="FNA"/> The [[flower]]s are borne in [[cyme (botany)|cymes]] of 1–5, arising from the axils of the higher leaves. Each flower is around {{convert|6|mm|abbr=on}} in diameter, with 10 [[stamen]]s, 3 [[Stigma (botany)|stigmas]], five lanceolate–triangular, green-coloured but scarious-margined [[sepal]]s, and five slightly shorter white [[petal]]s.<ref name="FNA"/> The petals are divided into two almost to their base with the two halves angled apart,<ref name="FNA"/> so that the two halves of each petal lie over parts of adjacent sepals.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.plant-identification.co.uk/skye/caryophyllaceae/stellaria-alsine.htm |title=Bog stitchwort, ''Stellaria uliginosa'' |work=West Highland Flora |last=Farmer |first=Carl |access-date=June 7, 2020}}</ref>

==Ecology==
Bog stitchwort grows in various types of [[wetland]] habitat; in the British Isles, it is especially characteristic of areas poached by cattle.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/plant/stellaria-uliginosa |title=''Stellaria uliginosa'' |work=Online Atlas of the British and Irish Flora |publisher=[[Biological Records Centre]] |access-date=June 7, 2020}}</ref> It flowers in spring and early summer.<ref name="FNA"/>

==Distribution==
Bog stitchwort is widespread in central and western Europe, but is rarer in eastern and southern Europe and the northern half of Scandinavia.<ref>{{cite book |series=Atlas Florae Europaeae |volume=3 |title=Distribution of Vascular Plants in Europe |year=1988 |editor1-first=Jaakko |editor1-last=Jalas |editor2-first=Juha |editor2-last=Suominen |publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] |isbn=978-0-521-34272-8 |page=76}}</ref> It is thought to be native to eastern parts of North America, but to be an [[introduced species]] in the Pacific Northwest.<ref name="FNA"/> It has also become naturalised in South America, in Asia, where it has become a weed of [[rice field]]s,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://gobotany.nativeplanttrust.org/species/stellaria/alsine/ |title=''Stellaria alsine'' Grimm, bog stitchwort |work=Go Botany |publisher=[[Native Plant Trust]] |access-date=June 7, 2020}}</ref> and on the [[Kerguelen Islands]] in the southern Indian Ocean, where it is an aggressive [[invasive species]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.iucngisd.org/gisd/species.php?sc=1277 |title=''Stellaria alsine'' |work=Global Invasive Species Database |publisher=[[International Union for Conservation of Nature]] |access-date=June 7, 2020 |author=Comité français de l'UICN (IUCN French Committee) & IUCN SSC Invasive Species Specialist Group (ISSG)}}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
''Stellaria alsine'' was first described by [[Johann Friedrich Carl Grimm]] in 1767.<ref name="FNA"/> The species has also been widely referred to under the [[junior synonym]] ''Stellaria uliginosa''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ukwildflowers.com/Web_pages/stellaria_alsine_bog_stitchwort.htm |title=''Stellaria alsine'', bog stitchwort |work=Wild Flowers of Europe, Australia, Ireland and Britain |first=Peter |last=Llewellyn |date=2012-02-12 |access-date=June 7, 2020}}</ref>
